correctness.rationale: For every fixed d>=2 the exact inverse Fourier transform of B_R is (2pi)^(-d/2)R^(d/2)r^(-d/2)J_(d/2)(Rr); the Bessel expansion uniformly for R=1+delta u yields leading a_d r^(-alpha) Re(e^{i(r-beta)}A_delta(delta r)) with alpha=(d+1)/2, beta=(d+1)pi/4, and error O(r^(-alpha-1)). The normalized W^(2,1) profile family gives |A(s)|<=C(1+s)^(-2) and |A(s)-1|<=C(delta+|s|), uniformly even for delta-dependent eta. For p=p_c-lambda/log(1/delta), alpha p_c=d and the leading radial weight is r^(-1+alpha lambda/L). The integrable Bessel remainder contributes o(L) to the Lp-power via Holder; r<1 costs O(1), r>delta^-1 costs O(1), and logarithmic boundary layers of relative thickness epsilon cost O(epsilon L). On delta^(-epsilon)<=r<=delta^(-(1-epsilon)), A=1+o(1), while periodic |cos|^p averages to Gamma((p+1)/2)/(sqrt(pi)Gamma((p+2)/2)) with O(1) weighted error. Setting t=log(r)/L gives C_d int_0^1 exp(alpha lambda t)dt. Constants are uniform on each compact lambda set, fixed d and a common W^(2,1) bound, including changing profiles. Independently written checks verify Fourier/Bessel normalization, 25 coefficient/crossover configurations, 12 3D ball inversion identities, six box-profile antiderivative identities and C_2/C_3 values; these finite checks are corroborative, not proof.
residual_risks: No finite computation establishes the universal limit; analytic proof relies on standard fixed-order Bessel asymptotic and uniform integration by parts, explicitly reconstructed.
The proof assumes regularity/nonnegativity/uniform family bound exactly as stated; it does not cover rough unbounded classes.

value.rationale: The critical index p_c=2d/(d+1) is intrinsically the borderline for integrability of the Fourier transform of the Euclidean ball; the reciprocal-logarithmic exponent window is its natural nontrivial crossover scale. Determining the sharp exponential-tilt profile C_d Phi_d(lambda) on both sides, uniformly for a nontrivial class of varying boundary mollifiers in every fixed d>=2, supplies a mathematically motivated exact universality law not mechanically determined by a single endpoint constant. The kernel/operator distinction is essential, and the theorem does not claim a general disc-multiplier bound.
residual_risks: The contribution is confined to radial boundary-coordinate smoothing and critical-window kernel Lp powers; it does not solve sharp Fourier-multiplier operator norms or fixed off-critical behavior.
